sex.evidence: Experiments were conducted on male and female C57 BL6 mice (n = 10, 5 female)

dosing.evidence: A dose of 2 mg/kg was delivered via an intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection (n = 5).

handling.evidence: Paper describes habituation to the treadmill setup but does not describe a separate experimenter-handling protocol.

group_housing.evidence: Animals were housed under a 12/12 h light-dark cycle with food and water available ad libitum.

day_night_flipped.evidence: Animals were housed under a 12/12 h light-dark cycle... Habituation and recordings were performed during the dark phase of the cycle. (Direction of cycle not specified.)

enrichment_housing.evidence: Animals were housed under a 12/12 h light-dark cycle with food and water available ad libitum.

judge_notes: Paper is an in vivo electrophysiology study: LFP and multi-unit/single-unit extracellular recordings from anterior cingulate cortex in head-fixed awake mice on a treadmill. Per rubric, neural recordings (in vivo electrophysiology, LFP, single-unit) are explicitly excluded — even in awake/behaving animals — because the primary outcome is neural activity, not behaviour.

Locomotion on the treadmill is mentioned only as a covariate check (Wilcoxon comparing running time baseline vs psilocybin) and is not analysed as a primary behavioural outcome in its own apparatus/paradigm. No standard behavioural assay (OFT, EPM, HTR test, etc.) is scored in the paper; the home-cage head-twitch observation is mentioned only as off-line dose verification done separately from the experiments presented, with no data reported.
Therefore no scorable behavioural assays are produced; assays array is empty. All three candidate models also returned empty assay arrays, confirming this judgment.

Day/night flipped scored not_reported (medium confidence): testing was during the dark phase, but the paper does not state whether the light cycle was reversed or whether dark-phase testing was under standard or reversed lighting.
